The instant misc. petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioners for quashing of FIR No.204/2022, Police Station Mahila Thana Ganganagar, for offences under Sections 376(2)(n), 354(c) and 506 of IPC.
After hearing learned counsel for the petitioners and taking into consideration the material available on record, I am not [2023:RJ-JD:35781] (2 of 2) [CRLMP-5189/2022] inclined to quash the FIR.

However, liberty is granted to the petitioner No.1 to file representation alongwith relevant documents and screenshots of the conversation that happened between petitioner No.1 and the Gopal Das vs State Of Rajasthan (2023:Rj-Jd:35781) on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56446440/

sentences.text: The Superintendent of Police and Investigating Officer shall take up all the facts as well as representation, if any, filed on behalf of the petitioner No.1 and complete the investigation by considering them strictly in accordance with law within a period of four weeks from the date of filing of the representation.
For a period of six weeks, petitioner No.1-Gopal Das shall not be arrested in connection with FIR No.204/2022, Police Station Mahila Thana Ganganagar.

So far as Petitioner No.2 and Petitioner No.3 are concerned, learned Public Prosecutor has submitted that offences against petitioner No.2-Krishana Rani and petitioner No.3-Pradeep Kumar have not been proved, therefore, the present misc. petition has become infructuous and dismissed accordingly qua petitioner No.2 and petitioner No.3.
The instant misc. petition filed by the petitioners is disposed of.
Stay petition is also disposed of.
